key_findings: DuckDB is SINGLE-WRITER per database file — multiple processes CANNOT write to the same .duckdb file concurrently. Second writer gets 'already opened by another process' error. This is critical for our architecture: archive-ingest, post-ingest-scorer, and freshness-watchdog all write to signals.duckdb from separate cron processes — they will fail when they overlap

Partition by month, not day — one table per logical dataset. DuckDB supports SET PARTITIONED BY (year(ts), month(ts)). Daily aggregation done in queries via DATE_TRUNC('day', ts), not separate daily tables

CHECKPOINT is the core maintenance mechanism — flushes WAL, reclaims space from deletes. Set wal_autocheckpoint higher (256-512MB) for write-heavy workloads to avoid constant I/O spikes from tiny default (16MB)
VACUUM ANALYZE refreshes statistics for query optimizer — matters for fast-changing tables on hot signals table. Run after significant data volume change
Parquet export for data > 90 days old — keeps DuckDB file small and fast. Partition Parquet exports by month for easy querying
For current scale (4434 events, ~few MB), no partitioning or checkpoint tuning needed yet. This research is PREVENTATIVE for when we hit millions of rows
